external_sources.title: Science Buddies Build the Best Paper Bridge
external_sources.supports: A flat paper sheet can be folded into a channel for a model bridge. The local 20 by 8 cm card plan is an authored choice. This pack covers identification and marking out only; building and testing occur in later scheme weeks.

evidence.description: Individual labelled plan plus an actual flat card blank marked at 2 cm and 6 cm from one long edge, with checked measurements, support and feedback response.

routes.Supported: Supported: ask an adult to steady the ruler.
routes.Independent: Independent: plan, mark and check each line.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain why both marks use one edge.

vocab.definition: A drawing or steps that guide our work.
Put lines or points on a material.
Find a size using a scale.
The side of a flat shape.
A mark that shows where to bend later.
Look again to see if work fits the plan.

cases.text: Draw the plan. Add 20 cm, 8 cm and the two fold lines.
cases.fact: A plan shows the intended size and marks.
cases.next_step: Label card as the material and ruler/pencil as tools.
cases.staff_note: Plan not to scale. Future model spans a 10 cm gap with 5 cm of its length on each support when centred.

cases.text: Check the flat card is 20 cm by 8 cm. Choose one long start edge.
cases.fact: Use a staff-cut blank of the agreed size.
cases.next_step: Label the chosen long edge with a small star.
cases.staff_note: Staff prepare accurate blanks. If the card differs from the plan, replace it or agree and record a revised plan before marking.

cases.text: Put ruler zero at the start edge. Mark 2 cm and 6 cm at one short end.
cases.fact: Both distances begin at the same long edge.
cases.next_step: Hold the ruler still and make two small pencil marks.
cases.staff_note: Adult may steady the ruler. Record what the pupil actually measures and marks; do not label adult marks independent.

cases.text: At the other short end, mark 2 cm and 6 cm from that same long edge.
cases.fact: Matching marks at both ends guide straight lines.
cases.staff_note: Do not measure the 6 cm point from the 2 cm point: both start from the starred long edge.

cases.text: Join the two 2 cm marks. Then join the two 6 cm marks. Use dash lines.
cases.fact: The two lines run along the card.
cases.next_step: Use the ruler as a straight edge. Label the lines fold.
cases.staff_note: The middle panel is 4 cm wide. The future side panels are each 2 cm. No folding today.

cases.text: Check the plan and marks. Add your ID. Store the card flat for next week.
cases.fact: Rechecking can catch a wrong mark.
cases.next_step: Correct a mark if needed and record the change.
cases.staff_note: Keep the actual marked blank or a clear process photo/work reference with consent and normal evidence procedures. No model building or load testing yet.

You Do evidence: 6 minutes.
Teacher: Use both Evidence Sheet pages. Plan: 20 cm length, 8 cm width, card material, two parallel fold lines 2 cm and 6 cm from the same long edge. Mark all four points on the actual card and join matching pairs. Distances between lines: 4 cm; side panels: 2 cm each. Check at both short ends against the ruler scale. Future centred 10 cm span leaves (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm overlap at each end. Record measured values and support; a drawing alone does not evidence marking out. Scribe without supplying the reason. Keep the actual work reference.

Monday 9–Friday 13 November 2026 · one 40-minute lesson
Exact scheme cells

This lesson supplies formative work. The scheme places building in Week 3 and testing/evaluation in Week 4; this pack does not claim a completed product or award. Public award labels are masked only.
Purpose and success checks
How can a clear plan guide our marks?
I can draw and label a simple plan. I can measure and mark fold lines on card. I can check my marks and ask for help.
LAUNCH-DT-W2-E1: Individual labelled plan plus an actual flat card blank marked at 2 cm and 6 cm from one long edge, with checked measurements, support and feedback response.
Before pupils arrive

Prepare one flat 20 cm by 8 cm card blank per learner plus spares, cut by staff beforehand. Supply a clear centimetre ruler, pencil, eraser and mat. Print the Evidence Sheet, Support Cards and Vocabulary Mat. Keep cutting tools away. Have a folder for named flat blanks.

Check local risk controls and individual access needs. Offer a quiet seat, processing time and help with grip or ruler control. Pupils may work beside a peer or with an adult; capture each person’s own work.
Calendar
W2 runs Monday 9 to Friday 13 November. The owner’s D&T allocation is one period a week. No fixed day or clock slot was supplied. Enter the actual date above.
Forty minute sequence
Slide
Min
Action
Open title and big question before timing.
Private check-in, clear work space, ask for support.
Name a clue in the diagram; read labels aloud.
Read the exact objective and success checks.
Model the materials/tools or marking sequence.
Read the hinge; obtain a letter and a reason.
Draw a plan; measure and mark the actual card.
Finish individual evidence and check the actual work.
Check name, help used and next step; return tools.
Take one quiet exit response; note next teaching need.
Keep the vocabulary mat available throughout.
Hidden reference for adults.
Hinge and reteach

C. Align the zero mark, not the ruler end or the 1 cm mark, with the chosen long edge. At each short end mark 2 cm and 6 cm from that same edge. Re-model on scrap card if needed, then let the learner make a fresh mark. Ask why A would give the wrong distance. A correct letter alone does not show understanding.
Access routes
Supported: ask an adult to steady the ruler. Independent: plan, mark and check each line. Aspire: explain why both marks use one edge.

Use slide 3 for the full plan and Support Cards page 3 for the marking guide. Pupils draw and label their own plan, then mark an actual staff-cut blank following A–F. Start page 1 evidence during practice. Watch zero alignment, the same start edge and matching points. Adults may steady a ruler but record assistance.

Begin evidence during the 12-minute practice and finish in the six-minute capture. Read or scribe the learner’s words. Record physical assistance precisely. No forced pair work, cold calling or public performance.
Safe work evidence and learner voice
Practical boundaries

Staff check the task and room risk assessment and individual access needs. Staff pre-cut clean, staple-free 20 by 8 cm card blanks before the lesson. Learners use only rulers, pencils and erasers to plan and mark. No pupil cutting, folding, assembly, load test, blades, hot glue or powered tools. Store marked blanks flat for Week 3.
Assessment and feedback

Plan: 20 cm length, 8 cm width, card material, two parallel fold lines 2 cm and 6 cm from the same long edge. Mark all four points on the actual card and join matching pairs. Distances between lines: 4 cm; side panels: 2 cm each. Check at both short ends against the ruler scale. Future centred 10 cm span leaves (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm overlap at each end. Record measured values and support; a drawing alone does not evidence marking out.

Keep the actual work, reason, response mode and support. A copied model or blank form is not completed evidence. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after actual banking.
Lundy moments

Space: a calm place and accessible materials. Voice: a choice or request for help. Audience: the adult listens, checks and replies. Influence: record the requested support or next task and the change made.
Speaking listening and writing

Possible communication evidence: Explain a plan, listen to the marking sequence, ask for the ruler to be steadied and describe a checked or corrected mark. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio. No communication criteria are assigned here.
Private help and reflection

Offer a quiet help request or an observation alternative. If a concern is disclosed, listen calmly, follow local safeguarding procedures and keep that record separate from lesson evidence. Do not promise secrecy.

Teacher model and hinge

Plan a card bridge: 20 cm long, 8 cm wide. Choose one long edge as the start edge. At one short end, put ruler zero on that edge. Mark 2 cm and 6 cm from that same edge. Repeat at the other short end. Join each pair. Check both lines. Keep the card flat.

C. Align the zero mark, not the ruler end or the 1 cm mark, with the chosen long edge. At each short end mark 2 cm and 6 cm from that same edge. Re-model on scrap card if needed, then let the learner make a fresh mark. Ask why A would give the wrong distance.
Individual evidence key

Plan: 20 cm length, 8 cm width, card material, two parallel fold lines 2 cm and 6 cm from the same long edge. Mark all four points on the actual card and join matching pairs. Distances between lines: 4 cm; side panels: 2 cm each. Check at both short ends against the ruler scale. Future centred 10 cm span leaves (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm overlap at each end. Record measured values and support; a drawing alone does not evidence marking out.
Feedback and safe teaching
Card A: Plan not to scale. Future model spans a 10 cm gap with 5 cm of its length on each support when centred.
Card B: Staff prepare accurate blanks. If the card differs from the plan, replace it or agree and record a revised plan before marking.
Card C: Adult may steady the ruler. Record what the pupil actually measures and marks; do not label adult marks independent.
Card D: Do not measure the 6 cm point from the 2 cm point: both start from the starred long edge.
Card E: The middle panel is 4 cm wide. The future side panels are each 2 cm. No folding today.
Card F: Keep the actual marked blank or a clear process photo/work reference with consent and normal evidence procedures. No model building or load testing yet.
Common misunderstandings

Start from zero on the scale, which may be inset from the ruler end. Both distances use the same long edge. A 6 cm mark is not 6 cm beyond the 2 cm mark. Dashed lines mean future folds, not cuts. A plan is not the actual marked card. Do not claim that the model is built, tested or strong yet.
Practical boundary

Staff check the task and room risk assessment and individual access needs. Staff pre-cut clean, staple-free 20 by 8 cm card blanks before the lesson. Learners use only rulers, pencils and erasers to plan and mark. No pupil cutting, folding, assembly, load test, blades, hot glue or powered tools. Store marked blanks flat for Week 3.
Response and next teaching step

If a reason is vague, return to the actual item or mark. Model on a different sample, then let the learner retry. Use the NS+ prompt and learner response in their own colour before recording R. E means evidence actually banked in the school's evidence record. Keep safeguarding records separate.
Assessment boundary
LAUNCH-DT-W2-E1 is formative evidence. Building is in Week 3, testing/evaluation in Week 4. This pack claims no completed product, criterion or award. Sources: FACTS_LEDGER.md.
